name: r6b_tou_bank_lead_follows_primary__v4
description: A time-of-use peak starts at 16:15. The house is at 72 F and banking toward 68 F means 4 F of cooling. v3's learned rate is slow (1 F per hour); v4's fitted AC is a realistic 3.5 F per hour (2.8 F in the first hour through the house's hidden mass), and on a 90 F afternoon the house leaks heat back in at 0.05 of the gap per hour. Primary engine v4 (v3 is the live comparison engine): the lead comes from v4's OWN house model (thermal mass and sun included), stepped with the AC fully on against the forecast, not from a first-order formula (Issue #1517). That model needs about 289 minutes (332 with the 1.15 safety factor), so the lead hits the 240-minute cap and the bank window opens at 12:15, before this scenario's 13:00 start. The bank is on from the first moment: the thermostat is told 68 F at 13:00 with no 76 F comfort write first, the plan names the 12:15 window, and the 13:05 check and the 14:00 and 14:20 cycles re-assert 68 F.

events.note: The 14:20 plan cycle (the bank window opened at 12:15 and is still running).
End of run: three minutes after the 14:25 check.

assertions.reason: The window (12:15) is already open when the scenario starts, so the bank applies at once.
The 13:00 setup tells the thermostat the 68 F bank setpoint, with no 76 F comfort write before the bank (issue #1393).
The 14:00 cycle inside the open bank re-asserts the 68 F bank setpoint once, without the 76 F comfort setpoint first.

The window the plan shows starts at the 240-minute cap: v4's own house model needs about 289 minutes (332 with the safety factor) to bank 4 F on this 90 F afternoon (Issue #1517; the first-order leak lead said 13:42, the leak-unaware lead 14:24, a v3 rate 12:15, the 45-minute default 15:30).
The plan list has no pre-cool step: the window opened at 12:15, before now, so it is already running.

verdict.summary: The time-of-use bank opens by the primary engine (v4) house model, and the plan and the thermostat agree on when
verdict.observed_behavior: Window 12:15 (the 240-minute cap; v4's model needs about 289 min raw, 332 min with the safety factor); 68 F written at 13:00 and re-asserted at 13:04:59, 14:00 and 14:20, with no 76 F comfort write before the bank.
verdict.expected_behavior: The house is banked when the peak starts: the lead is v4's own house model (thermal mass, sun, leak), which sees what a first-order formula misses on a hot afternoon (Issue #1517). Re-derived 2026-11-11 with the owner's approval (second re-derivation for #1517): the previous 13:42 start (153 min, first-order leak formula) was too late for v4's model, which needs about 289 min raw / 332 min with the 1.15 safety factor; the 240-minute cap now applies (the owner estimated about 315). Even the cap is shorter than the model's need - tracked separately.

source: synthetic: Issue #1230 R6b (primary prediction engine drives decisions), redesigned per the independent review; DP-11 pending, unsigned
